lead_raw_text:
The structure of Mg12Ni2Fe2 (Mg6NiFe) crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Amm2 (No. 38), with 16 atoms per unit cell distributed over six independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows all Fe, Mg, and Ni centers adopt a close-packed-like local arrangement with 12 geometric neighbors per atom, with neighbor distances ranging from about 2.73 to 3.23 Å. The neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component spanning all 16 sites. Validated polyhedron-sharing relations indicate that 12-vertex Mg-centered polyhedra exhibit corner-, edge-, and face-sharing, while Mg–Ni and Mg–Fe polyhedra show corner- and edge-sharing.
